title: You Sit Completely Still, Yet Watching Someone Grab Food Fires Your Motor Cortex
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Giacomo Rizzolatti, Luciano Fadiga & Gallese (1992-1996): Parma Premotor Area F5 'Mirror Neurons' & Greg Hickok's Critique, grounded in G. di Pellegrino, L. Fadiga, L. Fogassi, V. Gallese et al. (1992) (Experimental Brain Research). Empirical findings show that in 1992 at the University of Parma, Giuseppe di Pellegrino, Luciano Fadiga, Leonardo Fogassi, Vittorio Gallese, and Giacomo Rizzolatti recorded single neurons in ventral premotor cortex (area F5) of macaques trained to pick up small food items like raisins or peanuts.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how premotor cortex, parietal cortex, temporal lobe coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that connected to an audio loudspeaker so every action potential sounded a crisp 'pop-pop-pop,' F5 neurons were thought to be purely motor command cells firing when the hand shaped a precision pinch or whole-hand grasp.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- G. di Pellegrino, L. Fadiga, L. Fogassi, V. Gallese et al. (1992). Understanding motor events: a neurophysiological study. Experimental Brain Research. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf00230027
- A. Compston (2009). Action recognition in the premotor cortex. By Vittorio Gallese, Luciano Fadiga, Leonardo Fogassi and Giacomo Rizzolatti. Brain 1996: 119; 593-609. Brain. https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/awp167
- L. Fogassi, V. Gallese, L. Fadiga, G. Luppino et al. (1996). Coding of peripersonal space in inferior premotor cortex (area F4). Journal of Neurophysiology. https://doi.org/10.1152/jn.1996.76.1.141
